name: app.farefacts/fare-facts
title: Fare Facts
description: Dated, sourced facts on US air passenger rights and how to read an airline ticket.

tools.name: list_rights_topics
tools.description: US airline passenger rights: list the topics Fare Facts covers (bumping/denied boarding, refunds for cancellations and schedule changes, delays, meals and hotels, tarmac delays, the 24-hour rule, bag fees, lost or damaged bags, bag tracing, wheelchairs and mobility devices, what sellers must disclose before you buy, and pending rule changes), each with its topic id and a one-line summary. Free: every Fare Facts tool and answer is free, with no account. Takes no input.

tools.name: get_passenger_right
tools.description: US airline passenger rights: the federal rule for one topic (for example refunds when a flight is cancelled, denied boarding, tarmac delays, the 24-hour rule, lost bags, wheelchairs), questions a passenger can raise with the airline, citations and a current-as-of date. It states rules only; it does not calculate bump payment amounts or explain ticket codes. Free: every Fare Facts tool and answer is free, with no account. Names, confirmation codes (record locators), ticket numbers and frequent flyer numbers are not needed or used; the input is only the codes or numbers in the input schema.

topic.description: Topic id; the allowed ids are the values listed in this schema.

tools.name: calculate_bump_compensation
tools.description: US airline passenger rights: denied boarding compensation calculator for an involuntary bump from an oversold flight under 14 CFR 250.5. Returns the tier (0%, 200% or 400%), the formula result and the cap applied, the right to cash instead of a voucher, the exceptions, and the regulation's definition of fare. It covers involuntary bumps only, not volunteers, who negotiate their own deal with the airline. Free: every Fare Facts tool and answer is free, with no account. Names, confirmation codes (record locators), ticket numbers and frequent flyer numbers are not needed or used; the input is only the codes or numbers in the input schema.

one_way_fare_usd.description: One-way fare in US dollars to the passenger's destination or first stopover (a planned break of more than 4 hours), including all mandatory taxes and fees but not optional extras such as seat or bag fees. This is how 14 CFR 250.1 defines "fare". An award or other zero-fare ticket is 0.

route.description: domestic = within the US; international_from_us = an international flight departing a US airport.

alternate_arrival_delay_hours.description: How many hours after the original flight's planned arrival the alternate flight the airline offered is planned to arrive (at the destination or first stopover). Omitted when no alternate flight was offered.

tools.name: explain_tax_codes
tools.description: US airline ticket taxes and fees: explain two-character tax codes from a ticket receipt (for example US, ZP, AY, XF, YC, XY, XA), with each amount, its effective date and its source (detail 'full' adds every note). Codes not in the verified list are reported as such, never guessed. Fare basis codes are not covered. Free: every Fare Facts tool and answer is free, with no account. Names, confirmation codes (record locators), ticket numbers and frequent flyer numbers are not needed or used; the input is only the codes or numbers in the input schema. The input is the codes alone, for example ["US","ZP","AY","XF"].

codes.description: 1 to 20 two-character tax codes from the ticket's tax box.

detail.description: Optional. "brief" (default) gives the main facts; "full" adds every note we have.

tools.name: explain_fare_basis
tools.description: US airline tickets, how to read them: explain a fare basis code (for example KL7NR3). Returns the booking class from the first letter, labeled notes that match the rest of the code (detail 'full' lists every convention), and a tip to paste the fare rules from your own booking for exact change and refund terms. Tax codes are not covered. Free: every Fare Facts tool and answer is free, with no account. Names, confirmation codes (record locators), ticket numbers and frequent flyer numbers are not needed or used; the input is only the codes or numbers in the input schema.

fare_basis.description: The fare basis code only, 1 to 15 characters.

airline.description: Optional 2-character airline code, for example AA, DL, UA or B6.

detail.description: Optional. "brief" (default) gives the main facts; "full" adds every note we have.

tools.name: get_missing_miles_link
tools.description: US airline frequent flyer programs: where and how to request missing miles or points for a past flight (American, Delta, United, JetBlue, Alaska/Hawaiian, Southwest, Frontier, Spirit), with the waiting period, deadline, login needs and a basic economy caveat. Passenger rights rules are not covered. Free: every Fare Facts tool and answer is free, with no account. Names, confirmation codes (record locators), ticket numbers and frequent flyer numbers are not needed or used; the input is only the codes or numbers in the input schema.

airline.description: The airline whose program you are asking about.
